What it means: Rental companies, vehicle leasing, fleet operators, car/van/truck operators.
Likely service need: Vehicle access, fleet funding, driver-ready vehicle programs, dealer/rental partner channels.
Campaign use: Lead with vehicle access and financing discovery; ask about platform compatibility and fleet size.
Validation note: Uber/Lyft vehicle programs and approved rental channels validate need for compliant vehicles.

What it means: Courier, delivery, transport, trucking, freight, route, shuttle, driver-oriented businesses.
Likely service need: Rental car, van/truck access, maintenance, insurance/registration, working capital.
Campaign use: Target as demand-side vehicle users; ask whether they need cars, vans, or driver onboarding support.
Validation note: Amazon Flex, DoorDash, and Instacart all have vehicle-access requirements or vehicle options by market.

What it means: Car wash, detailing, repair, towing, tire, smog, registration, dealer and service businesses.
Likely service need: Referral partner, local lead generation, website, credit/funding, customer acquisition.
Campaign use: Target as partner channel and service vendor for drivers/owners needing vehicle support.
Validation note: This is a partner lane, not just a customer lane.

What it means: New businesses, owner-operated filings, capital-intensive operations, equipment-heavy services.
Likely service need: Business funding readiness, credit-readiness discovery, vehicle/equipment financing prep.
Campaign use: Use discovery language only; no approval or credit-repair guarantee language.
Validation note: SBA materials support funding and business-credit planning as normal small-business launch needs.

What it means: New entities with no website/email, consumer-facing services, brand/name-driven businesses.
Likely service need: Website, domain/email, CRM intake, Google/online presence, lead-capture pages.
Campaign use: Use as first enrichment step and as a sellable service lane after owner match is verified.
Validation note: SBA business-name and marketing materials support online presence as a launch activity.

What it means: Tech, software, computers, devices, systems, managed service, security, electronics, multi-device operations.
Likely service need: Device/software inventory, procurement, asset lifecycle, security hygiene, workspace setup.
Campaign use: Target entities with IT/tech keywords and companies that likely need device/software asset tracking.
Validation note: NIST ITAM guidance supports managing physical and virtual assets as a risk/operations need.

What it means: Broad new LLC/corporation filings without direct auto/tech keywords.
Likely service need: Funding readiness, website/email setup, compliance/admin checklist, vehicle/asset discovery.
Campaign use: Nurture campaigns only; enrich before high-touch outbound.
Validation note: Not every business needs every service; use filing behavior to choose the first ask.
